prerequisites: All Thomas More students can apply for this elective course.
Selection is based on an intake interview.
Only a limited number of students can participate in this course.

learning_outcomes.text: You articulate in a personal presentation how the bootcamp has broadened your perspective on global challenges and reflect on your role as a global citizen within a diverse society.
You communicate professionally and culturally sensitively with local and international partners during the bootcamp/COIL and clearly present your insights to an external jury.
You expand your professional network through interactions with local students, entrepreneurs, and coaches, and utilize relevant contacts during the bootcamp/COIL.
You reflect on your own actions and intercultural collaboration and summarize these personal insights in a presentation for a jury.
You identify personal growth opportunities based on feedback and reflection, and formulate concrete actions for your professional development in a personal presentation.
You investigate how social entrepreneurship contributes to sustainable development and integrate this perspective into the pitch of a social business idea.
You contribute constructively to the team process with local students, take responsibility for joint assignments, and work solution-oriented on the business model.

syllabus_topics: Option A: Collaboration with OVO (Ondernemers voor ondernemers) for entrepreneurial trips to Africa (Uganda: Kampala; Rwanda: tbc)
Student immersion in the social and entrepreneurial context of Ugandan culture.
Student coaching of a local social entrepreneur (startup or scale up) with a senior OVO coach.
Day 1: Historical and cultural city tour of Kampala (Uganda) or Kigali (Rwanda).
Day 2: Visit to startups and social organizations in the capital.
Day 3: Visit to startups and/or scale ups outside the capital.
Days 4-6: SusTech4Africa Boostcamp with 10 local entrepreneurs from various sectors/industries.
Option B: Collaboration with MUBS (Makerere University Business School Kampala- Uganda) for an entrepreneurial trip to Uganda (Kampala).
Student immersion in the social and entrepreneurial context of Ugandan culture.
Student works in a team with local entrepreneurial students on the business model of a social & entrepreneurial concept.
Day 1: Historical and cultural city tour of Kampala.
Day 2: Visit to startups and social organizations in the capital.
Day 3: Teambuilding activities with local students.
Days 4-6: Impact Bootcamp with 20 teams of student entrepreneurs from MUBS.
Option C: COIL: collaborative online international learning (acceleration program @ MUBS).
Student works online in collaboration with the MUBS student team from 'business model' to 'investment readiness'.
assessment_rules: The assessment is based on a 1-20 point scale. The process counts for 50% and the presentation for 50%. There is no second examination opportunity and no resit is possible for this course.
